headword: {始|はじ}め{良|よ}ければ{終|お}わり{良|よ}し
reading: はじめよければおわりよし
gloss: all's well that begins well; a good start makes a good end

definitions.gloss: all's well that begins well; a good start makes a good end
definitions.explanation: A proverb meaning that if something begins smoothly, the rest will go well too. Often cited to encourage care and attention at the very start of a task or project.

examples.japanese: {始|はじ}め{良|よ}ければ{終|お}わり{良|よ}しと{言|い}う。
examples.english: As they say, all's well that begins well.

examples.japanese: {始|はじ}め{良|よ}ければ{終|お}わり{良|よ}しだから、{最初|さいしょ}が{肝心|かんじん}だ。
examples.english: Since a good start makes a good end, the very beginning is what matters.

examples.japanese: {始|はじ}め{良|よ}ければ{終|お}わり{良|よ}しと{言|い}うように、{新|あたら}しいプロジェクトの{立|た}ち{上|あ}げには{特|とく}に{気|き}を{使|つか}いたい。
examples.english: As the proverb "all's well that begins well" says, I want to be especially careful when launching a new project.

notes:
A proverb often quoted in business and educational settings to stress the importance of a careful start. Frequently introduced with {〜|〜}と{言|い}うように or {〜|〜}と{言|い}うとおり to lead into the speaker's main point.

USAGE:
- Often used as encouragement at the start of a new venture
- May serve as a self-reminder before beginning preparation work
- Sometimes used reflectively after a project succeeded thanks to a strong opening
The phrase corresponds closely to the English title and proverb "All's well that ends well" — but reversed. The Japanese version emphasizes the start as the cause; the English version emphasizes the ending as what ultimately matters. The two are not interchangeable in nuance.

RELATED WORDS:
- {終|お}わり{良|よ}ければ{全|すべ}て{良|よ}し: all's well that ends well — the more direct counterpart to the English proverb
